meta.note: Educational comparison, not a prediction, not an official evacuation plan and not a buyout proposal. Households and residents are synthetic (the simulator's allocation of Genasys zone populations); a block is a street segment; no parcels, owners or addresses are used. "Still home when the fire front or embers arrived" counts synthetic people at that moment; it is not a casualty count. Costs are screening ranges, not an appraisal, policy or legal analysis.
meta.plan: DEFAULT_PLAN (first order 10 min after ignition, status-quo parking), each scenario's default time of day
meta.blockRule: derived: A block is one street segment of data/model/network.json on which js/sim.js places households (drivable, not a freeway or ramp, in an evacuation zone), in City Fire Zones 2–3 or, outside Berkeley, at 90 m elevation or higher (the simulator's hill proxy). Ranked if it holds at least 1 expected household.

provenance.expectedHouseholds: synthetic: zone population (Genasys, or 2020 Census where data/assumptions.json says so) spread over street length as js/sim.js does, / 2.37 persons per household; expected values
provenance.front: derived from synthetic runs: share of runs (among runs where the block has at least one household) in which at least one household was still home when the fire front reached the block
provenance.ember: derived from synthetic runs: same, when embers arrived
provenance.cut: derived from synthetic runs: share of runs in which at least one of the block's cars was on a street when the fire front reached it, or ended the run on the road with no route to safety
provenance.engine: derived from synthetic runs: share of runs in which no engine reaches the block within the City's 5-minute standard at ignition, status-quo parking (js/sim.js engineReachTimes; parked cars depend on seed and day or night)
provenance.nest: derived: number of dead-end access areas in series between the block and an exit (data/model/access-constraints.json; one-way chokes left out)
provenance.choke: derived, capped at 1: vehicles behind the block's outermost dead-end choke ÷ the choke segment's capacity per lane (veh/h), i.e. hours of choke capacity the area's cars need
provenance.score: model rule: 3 × front + 1 × ember + 2 × cut + 1 × engine + 0.5 × nest + 1 × choke (no calibration; the components are shown so a reader can re-sort)
